title: docs: the ObjectUI protocol pages claim native mobile rendering and offline-first mobile apps that the platform does not deliver
body:
Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/mobile#150

The maintainer asked for this design's cards to be filed but not dispatched yet (verbatim: 「开卡，不要派发」). objectstack-ai/mobile#150 is the release gate.

## Defect

Customer-facing docs advertise capabilities the runtime does not deliver, which AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10 forbids (declared ≠ delivered):

- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx` ~line 183: "Mobile app? Same YAML file renders natively (zero code)".
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/index.mdx` ~lines 495–515, "Offline-First Mobile Apps":
  - it shows a `mobile_renderer: { offline_cache, sync_strategy }` block, which is no metadata key the spec declares;
  - it attaches dollar savings figures to it.
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx` ~lines 245–285: the server-driven-UI diagram describes a mobile app with a generic native renderer.

Re-check: `grep -n "renders natively\|Offline-First Mobile\|mobile_renderer\|Mobile App Bundle" content/docs/protocol/objectui/*.mdx`

## Reality

The ObjectOS mobile app (objectstack-ai/mobile 2.0) is a native shell that hosts the web Console. Phones get the same Console renderer as browsers, so "one definition, every screen" is still true, but through the Console, not a native renderer. There is no offline mobile renderer.

## Ask

- Rewrite those passages to state what is delivered: one definition rendered by the Console on desktop and phone, and the mobile app hosting the Console.
- Delete the `mobile_renderer` example and the unmeasured savings figures.
- Keep the server-driven-UI argument, which still holds for the Console.

## Acceptance

The re-check grep returns nothing that promises native rendering or offline mobile.
